absent: Invalidation filter computation and shared-state tracking rules are not shown in these fragments.
Folio acquisition, private versus shared accounting, and architecture reclaim behavior are not shown.
Binding creation, memslot update synchronization beyond release, and active file reference semantics are not shown.
IRQ routing table layout, MSI dispatch internals, and architecture irqchip predicate internals are not shown.
Halt polling algorithm, statistics layouts, preemption operations, and kick mask usage are not shown.
MMU lock implementation, remote TLB flush, unmap handler, page-cache cache invalidation, and notifier end pairing are not shown.
Supported guest memfd flags, mapping support predicate, and filesystem mount setup are not shown.

findings.text: Guest memfd creation entry validates caller supplied size and flags then delegates to an internal creator. Flags outside the supported set are rejected, size must be positive and page aligned, otherwise creation proceeds and returns a descriptor or a negative error.

Userspace MSI injection entry validates that the VM uses an in-kernel irqchip and that supplied flags carry no bits beyond the device id allowance, copies address, data, flags and device id into a kernel routing entry, then dispatches it with the userspace source identity.

IRQ routing initialization allocates a routing table sized for a single entry, marks it as holding one entry, initializes the irqchip pin mapping to an empty state, and publishes the table through the VM routing pointer with RCU semantics.

Two architecture overridable predicates default to allowing the operation: the irq routing permission check and the shared initialization support check for guest memory both report true when no architecture override is present.

Guest memfd fallocate only supports size-preserving operations. Requests lacking the keep-size behavior or carrying any other mode besides keep-size and hole punch are rejected as unsupported, and offset and length must both be page aligned.

Allocation rejects any range extending beyond current file size as invalid. Within size it walks folios from start to end, aborting with interruption status if a signal is pending, stopping on folio acquisition failure, advancing by folio span, releasing each folio after use, and yielding scheduling opportunity between iterations.

Hole punch converts byte offset and length to page indices by shifting, then performs ordered invalidation start, page cache truncation over the byte range, and invalidation end while bindings are held stable, always reporting success.

User mapping fault fails with bus error when the fault offset lies at or beyond file size or when the page is not in shared state. Otherwise it obtains the backing folio, requests retry on temporary unavailability, converts other acquisition failures to fault errors, rejects large folios, ensures up to date content by clearing a fresh page, and installs the corresponding page with locked status.

Mapping requires underlying file support for mapping and requires both shared mapping flags to be present. On success it installs a dedicated virtual memory operations table. Policy hooks route set and lookup operations to per-inode shared policy storage, using inode number as index identifier and returning null when no explicit policy exists.

Internal creation obtains an unused descriptor, allocates per-file state, pins the file operations, creates a secure anonymous inode named for guest memory, marks it regular with given size, applies high-user reclaim and inaccessible mapping attributes, records flags, wraps it in a read-write pseudo file linked to per-file state, registers the binding structure and list membership, and unwinds in reverse order on failure.

Inode slab handling separates one-time object setup from per-instance setup. One-time setup only initializes the embedded VFS inode. Per-instance allocation initializes shared policy, clears flags, and initializes the file list. Destruction releases shared policy and freeing returns the container to the slab cache.

Host address range handling rejects empty ranges, requires at least one of handler or lock callback to be present, forbids a lock callback in lockless mode, then scans each address-space memslot interval tree for overlap, clips to slot bounds, translates to guest frame numbers with shared-only filtering, invokes the handler per overlap, and optionally flushes remote TLBs when work was reported.

A null callback marker and its predicate identify the placeholder function. Aging helpers build a notifier range with caller supplied bounds and handler, no lock callback, configurable flush behavior, non-blocking semantics, and lockless mode selected by build configuration, then delegate to the common range walker and return its outcome without flush in the no-flush variant.

Virtual CPU initialization sets up mutual exclusion, marks no running CPU, links the owning VM and identifier, clears process tracking, initializes process lock and wait and async fault state, clears spin-loop and eligibility and preemption and readiness flags, registers preemption notification, clears last used slot, and formats a statistics identifier from creator process id and virtual CPU id. Shadow flush delegates to architecture flush plus reclaim notification. Kick acknowledgement is a no-op.

Guest memory operations serialize against truncation using filemap invalidation locks: hole punch and release hold exclusive protection across paired invalidation, allocation and memory-error handling hold shared protection while walking or notifying, keeping paired notifications matched.

Release path holds the VM slot mutex and the filemap invalidation lock while clearing guest memory file pointers in all bound slots with single-store semantics, issuing a full-range invalidation, and removing list membership, then releases locks before destroying binding storage, freeing file state, and dropping the VM reference.

Per-file invalidation end acquires the VM MMU lock and issues an MMU end notification only when the binding index contains a present entry overlapping the notified range; otherwise it performs no locking. Start fan-out iterates all files attached to the inode with a filter derived from the inode.

Range walker holds source-read protection across the address-space scan and acquires the MMU lock once on first overlapping memslot when not lockless, invoking the optional lock callback at that point and skipping handler invocation when handler is the null placeholder, then releases the MMU lock and source protection at the end.

MMU notifier invalidation start increments an active invalidation counter under a dedicated spinlock to stabilize slot membership across paired start and end, invalidates guest frame to host page caches before acquiring MMU protection, then runs the unmapping range handler and notifies architecture reclaim only when a memslot overlapped.

Notifier range descriptor carries 64-bit start and end supporting both host virtual and guest physical spaces, a union argument, a guest frame handler pointer, a lock callback pointer, and flags for flush on success, blocking allowance, and lockless walk.

Range walk result carries two booleans reporting whether the handler reported work and whether any memslot overlapped. A small helper derives the owning VM from the embedded notifier via container relationship.

Guest memory defines virtual memory operations for fault plus optional NUMA policy hooks, file operations for mapping, generic open, release and fallocate, address space operations for no-op dirty, failing migrate, error handling and conditional reclaim on free, and inode operations where attribute change is always rejected.

Guest memory filesystem provides super operations for simple statfs and custom inode alloc, destroy and free, a filesystem context initializer selecting the guest memory magic and installing those operations, and a filesystem type naming the filesystem and binding context initialization with anonymous super teardown.

Invalidation follows paired start and end states: punch wraps truncation, memory error wraps notification without truncation and reports delayed handling to leave policy to userspace, and release issues a full-range pair after clearing bindings without freeing inode-backed pages, leaving later guest access to surface poison errors.

Fault handling moves from bounds and sharing checks to folio acquisition, then to retry, error conversion, large rejection, content initialization, or locked installation with cleanup on non-locked outcomes. Creation moves through descriptor, file state, operations pin, inode, file wrapper and registration states with reverse-order unwind on any failure.

Virtual filesystem entry points exposed are mapping, fallocate, fault, shared policy set and lookup, folio migrate and memory-error hooks, attribute set, inode alloc destroy and free, filesystem context initialization, and guest memfd creation plus userspace MSI injection, irq routing initialization, and MMU notifier invalidation start.

Hazards include folio reference leaks if unlock and put are skipped, spurious success if invalidation pairing is unbalanced, use after close if slot file pointers are dereferenced without active-file protection, lost wakeups if allocation ignores pending signals, silent corruption if large folios are installed, and guaranteed failures for migrate and attribute changes that callers must not treat as retryable.

Range walking hazards include imbalanced MMU progress accounting if slot membership changes between notifier start and end, missed TLB flush if flush-on-result is omitted when the handler reported work, and illegal lock callback use in lockless walks; empty ranges and doubly null callbacks are treated as programming errors.

ABI and tuning constants observed are integer to string buffer length twelve, halt polling defaults of grow factor two, grow start ten thousand, shrink factor two, and VM lifecycle event identifiers zero for create and one for destroy.

Compatibility handling provides two macro variants selecting either a caller supplied compat handler or rejecting compat ioctls and opens for compat tasks. Global state includes a VM list mutex, a virtual CPU slab cache, read-mostly preemption operations, per-CPU running virtual CPU pointer and kick mask, debug filesystem directory, per-VM statistics operations, active and total VM counters, halt polling interval, and unsafe mapping allowance.
